source_title: Measuring quality indicators in the operating room: cleaning and turnover time
locator: Abstract; cleaning-time sample and reported mean
source_setting: 25-room academic surgical center in the interior of São Paulo State, Brazil; about 2,177 surgeries/month and 73/day.
source_n: 101 operations for cleaning duration; 60 operations for interval between cases.
source_evidence_basis: Author-reported mean from observed cleaning-time sample (101 surgeries).
limitations: Single university hospital; exact observation dates and dispersion are not reported in the abstract. Cleaning time is concurrent with other turnover activity, not equivalent to full room turnover.
inferred_scenario_use: Use only as an external cleaning-task benchmark; do not treat as a local measured value or add it mechanically to turnover because tasks may overlap.

source_title: Improving Operating Room Turnover in Robotic Surgery: A Human Factors Approach
locator: Abstract; task-time breakdown of 20 observed pre-intervention turnovers
source_setting: Robotic-surgery operating rooms at one tertiary hospital; United States (city not stated in accessible abstract).
source_period: Pre-intervention observations Jan–Apr 2018; post-intervention observations Jan–Jun 2019.
source_n: 40 observed robotic turnovers: 20 pre-intervention and 20 post-intervention.
source_evidence_basis: Direct observation of 20 pre-intervention turnovers; abstract reports mean task time.
limitations: Robotic cases at one tertiary hospital; small sample and workflow-specific. Abstract does not report SD/range for these task values. Retrieval time is not general interfacility patient transport.
inferred_scenario_use: Treat as an external task-level scenario range anchor for resource-constrained OR sequencing; do not transplant robotic workflow durations as local averages.

source_title: Effect of a newly designed observation, response and discharge chart in the Post Anaesthesia Care Unit on patient outcomes: a quasi-experimental study in Australia
locator: Results; overall PACU LOS distribution and Figure 3A phase comparison
source_setting: PACU of an Australian hospital; the study included two implementation phases.
source_period: Two study phases; exact calendar dates not stated in the source summary. Overall sample spans both phases.
source_n: 1,417 PACU patients overall (63/1,417 had stay >2 hours).
quantity: PACU length of stay, overall median
source_evidence_basis: Observed PACU admission-to-discharge stay; source reports median 49.0 min (95% CI 47.7–50.3).
limitations: One hospital; PACU stay includes clinical recovery and operational discharge processes. Not a fixed service-time requirement.
inferred_scenario_use: Use as external context for PACU occupancy simulation; model clinical recovery and bed/transport holds as distinct processes where local data permit.

locator: Results; proportion of patients staying >2 hours
source_setting: PACU of an Australian hospital; the study included two implementation phases.
source_period: Two study phases; exact calendar dates not stated in the source summary. Overall sample spans both phases.
source_n: 1,417 PACU patients overall (63/1,417 had stay >2 hours).
source_evidence_basis: Observed proportion 63/1,417 (4.4%) remained in PACU >2 hours.
limitations: Single hospital and patient mix; duration threshold is not a measure of delay cause.
inferred_scenario_use: Can inform a rare long-occupancy scenario branch, with explicit external-proxy label and sensitivity analysis.

source_title: A work systems analysis of sterile processing: sterilization and case cart preparation
source_setting: Two sterile-processing facilities at a 700-bed academic medical center serving 56 clinics, 31 operating rooms and nine ambulatory centers, United States.
source_period: Observational data collection dates not specified in abstract; paper reports performance sampling and analysis of administrative tray-defect data.
source_n: 108 interruptions observed during case-cart preparation; 13.5 interruptions/hour reported
source_evidence_basis: Direct observation; article reports 108 interruptions, equivalent to 13.5 per hour, primarily phone calls.
limitations: Focused observation at one academic center; interruptions are not themselves delays or missed case starts. Administrative defect data represent a separate sample.
inferred_scenario_use: Represent sterile-processing case-cart work as interruption-prone and include a sensitivity parameter for interruptions; not a local event-rate estimate.

source_title: A work systems analysis of sterile processing: sterilization and case cart preparation
source_setting: Two sterile-processing facilities at a 700-bed academic medical center serving 56 clinics, 31 operating rooms and nine ambulatory centers, United States.
source_period: Observational data collection dates not specified in abstract; paper reports performance sampling and analysis of administrative tray-defect data.
quantity: Cases with at least one defective tray
source_evidence_basis: Retrospective administrative tray-defect dataset: 3,900 defects / 41,799 cases; authors report 9.3% with >=1 defective tray.
limitations: One academic center; a tray defect is not necessarily a delayed case, and defect categories include process issues beyond turnaround duration.
inferred_scenario_use: Use only to motivate a scenario branch in which instrument readiness can fail; do not equate defect rate with OR delay probability.
